    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_79/training_6.csv"
]

# Target schema columns and their types (for reference and enforcement)
target_columns = [
    'matricula', 'nome_discente', 'sexo', 'ano_ingresso', 'periodo_ingresso',
    'forma_ingresso', 'tipo_discente', 'status', 'sigla_nivel_ensino',
    'nivel_ensino', 'id_curso', 'nome_curso', 'modalidade_educacao',
    'id_unidade', 'nome_unidade', 'id_unidade_gestora', 'nome_unidade_gestora'
]

# Data types to enforce after loading and concatenation
# Using pandas dtypes where possible; for string columns, use 'string' dtype (pandas >=1.0)
dtype_map = {
    'matricula': 'float64',
    'nome_discente': 'string',
    'sexo': 'string',
    'ano_ingresso': 'Int64',  # nullable integer dtype
    'periodo_ingresso': 'float64',
    'forma_ingresso': 'string',
    'tipo_discente': 'string',
    'status': 'string',
    'sigla_nivel_ensino': 'string',
    'nivel_ensino': 'string',
    'id_curso': 'float64',
    'nome_curso': 'string',
    'modalidade_educacao': 'string',
    'id_unidade': 'float64',
    'nome_unidade': 'string',
    'id_unidade_gestora': 'float64',
    'nome_unidade_gestora': 'string'
}

# Step 1: Load all source CSV files into a list of DataFrames
dfs = []
for file_path in source_files:
    df = pd.read_csv(file_path, index_col=0, dtype=str)  # read all as string first to avoid dtype issues
    # Ensure all target columns exist in the source (they do, per prompt)
    # Select only target columns to avoid any extra columns
    df = df[target_columns].copy()
    dfs.append(df)

# Step 2: Concatenate all DataFrames (UNION) since all have the same schema as target
combined_df = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True)

# Step 3: Convert columns to appropriate types according to target schema
# Handle numeric conversions carefully, allowing for missing values
for col, dtype in dtype_map.items():
    if dtype == 'float64':
        combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce')
    elif dtype == 'Int64':  # nullable integer
        combined_df[col] = pd.to_numeric(combined_df[col], errors='coerce').astype('Int64')
    elif dtype == 'string':
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('string')
    else:
        # fallback: convert to string if unknown dtype
        combined_df[col] = combined_df[col].astype('string')

# Step 4: Export the combined DataFrame to the target CSV path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length6_79/target_multisource_cot.csv"
combined_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

df = pd.merge(source0, source1, on='matricula', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_1'))

df = pd.merge(df, source2, on='matricula', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_2'))

# Join with source3
df = pd.merge(df, source3, on='matricula', how='inner', suffixes=('', '_3'))

# Join with source5

# Join with source6

# After joining, columns with suffixes _1, _2, ... _6 are duplicates of the same columns.
